prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A glossary of very long German compounds: each row pairs an identifier-like headword (Begriff) with a short abbreviation (Kurzform) and a prose explanation (Erklärung). The reader looks up a term, checks its short form, then reads the explanation — so the table is scanned row by row, not column by column, and the headword is the anchor that must remain recognisable.","reading":"Vertical scan down column 1 to find the term, a quick glance at column 2 (a lookup key, not read as text), then a horizontal read of column 3 as running prose. Because col 1 entries are 300–546px unbreakable strings, at 360px they will break mid-word no matter what; the real choice is how much of that damage to absorb versus how much readable measure to give the prose and how much horizontal scrolling to impose.","groups":["col 1 (Begriff) and col 2 (Kurzform) form one unit — the term and its label, read together as the row's identity; they should sit adjacent and tight.","col 3 (Erklärung) is a separate register: continuous prose that only needs a workable measure, and it benefits from a clear gap after the identifier pair."],"keep_intact":["Kurzform values — short abbreviations (≤83px); splitting them destroys their meaning, so this column must never go below ~104px.","Begriff headwords ideally whole (546px worst case), which is only possible with a wide column / horizontal scroll.","Hyphenated compounds such as 'Kraftfahrzeug-Haftpflichtversicherung' should break at the hyphen, not mid-morpheme."],"may_wrap":["Erklärung — multi-clause prose (one-line 1091px); it wraps naturally and its row height can absorb 2–5 lines without harming the row's unity.","The longest Begriff strings, if the column is kept narrow; each row already has spare vertical height, so 2–3 line headwords remain scannable."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [205, 104, 295] · table 605×743px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 129, 129, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 245px
Design r2B: widths [180, 104, 340] · table 625×627px · row heights [36, 106, 83, 106, 106, 83, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 265px
Design r2C: widths [245, 104, 295] · table 645×743px · row heights [36, 129, 106, 129, 129, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/3 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 285px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
